Hyperinflation refers to a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy that is not directly attributable to changes in demand or supply. When a country experiences hyperinflation, it typically leads to a significant decrease in purchasing power for its citizens, as prices soar dramatically. This can result in widespread economic hardship, including increased unemployment, financial instability, and reduced living standards.

Hyperinflation occurs when the central bank lowers interest rates to encourage borrowing, which drives up consumption and production. As demand increases, prices rise, leading to further inflation. The process continues until the economy is unable to control the rate of inflation, and it becomes unsustainable. At this point, many countries default on their debts and enter into a period of hyperinflation.
